title: How about we compromise and let Lea Michele and Hannah Cruz switch ro...
transcript: it's hard for me to talk about this Broadway revival of Chess starring Lea Michele, Aaron Tveit, and Nicholas Christopher without talking about the concert version they did 3 years ago to test the waters for this run not just cause it's my main point of comparison but I think the specific differences between them perfectly illustrate where this revival went wrong in development. the thing that keeps coming to my mind is that the production has lost a sense of bite and a sense of high melodrama that I think could make the show work I do attribute that mostly to Michael Mayer’s direction but he also directed the 2022 concert which I liked a lot more, so what gives? some of it is definitely the cast and yes it has to be acknowledged that Lea Michele is probably one of the big ticket-buying draws that allowed this to come to Broadway in the first place but the performance itself, for me, is such a massive downgrade from Lena Hall in the concert version her rockstar voice and scrappy energy perfectly matched the vibe of the material whereas I think Lea Michele is playing it too straight and naturalistic and in this bombastic show it makes her performance feel kind of limp by comparison similarly, Aaron Tveit captures Freddy's confidence but not his volatility and even though Darren Criss could barely sing this role, frankly he had this manic petulance that made me really believe that he was a live wire and there's just none of that in Aaron Tveit’s performance Nicholas Christopher on the other hand comes out not only unscathed but with quite a star turn partly because the role lends itself to being played more straight forward but also I think he was just acting circles around these two. when it comes to the Arbiter's self-aware narration schtick I, for some reason, really liked it in 2022 and not at all here I wanna say it felt a little weirder and more commanding before almost like being played with a wink and a smile whereas now it's being played with a shrug and a laugh which just kind of undercuts the drama and makes it hard to get invested another thought I had while watching this revival is that maybe the show just lends itself better to concert stagings not just because the book is inferior to the score which it is - the score is by far the best part of this whole thing but because the book feels overly subservient to these hyper presentational songs almost like a jukebox musical, but not so I understand why it's often done in concert and I get the temptation from Michael Mayer to stage this production almost like a concert staging and I've heard a lot of criticism about the sparse staging of this production and to be honest it didn't bother me that much. I think it could have worked fine if the rest of the pieces were in place, so to speak but I'll admit that at its core the staging kind of has the same problem as the performances and the tone which is that if they were going for slick and polished it kinda came across flat and sterile instead. I wanna see a production of Chess that feels like a mix of opera and messy reality TV let's make it histrionic let's have people crawling on the floor screaming, crying, spitting there is some of that here, but for me not enough having said that I have to admit that Chess is a very interesting piece of musical theatre history and this is probably the last revival we're gonna get for a very very long time and between the score and certain performances like Nicholas Christopher, Hannah Cruz there are things to like about it so if you're interested in the lore of Chess and interested in seeing the first Broadway revival just kind of for science you know, it *might* be worth a visit
